# DestroyTargetForID

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to perform device destruction.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void DestroyTargetForID (
 SCSIDeviceIdentifiertargetID ); 
```

## Parameters

- `targetID`: SCSIDeviceIdentifier of desired targetID.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For HBA child classes that report true to the DoesHBAPerformDeviceManagement() method, the child class will be responsible for all device management by using these methods; otherwise, the superclass will be responsible for all device management. This method must be used to perform SCSI Parallel Device destruction and cannot be overridden.

Queries the HBA child class to determine if it automatically performs AutoSense and provides AutoSense data for each I/O. If the HBA allocates space for AutoSense in its HBA specific data region on a per task basis, the HBA should respond true.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool DoesHBAPerformAutoSense (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Return true if HBA performs AutoSense into its own private data buffer.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Queries the HBA child class to determine if it automatically performs AutoSense and provides AutoSense data for each I/O. If the HBA allocates space for AutoSense in its HBA specific data region on a per task basis, the HBA should respond true.

# DoesHBAPerformDeviceManagement

Determine if HBA will manage devices.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool DoesHBAPerformDeviceManagement (
 void ) = 0; 
```

return true means objects for target devices will only be created when the child class calls the CreateTargetForID method.

# ExecuteParallelTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

Submit a SCSIParallelTask for execution.

## Declaration

```objectivec
SCSIServiceResponse ExecuteParallelTask ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelRequest ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelRequest`: is a reference to the SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier to be executed.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

is an appropriate SCSIServiceResponse which are defined in the file \<IOKit/scsi/SCSITask.h\>.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The ExecuteParallelTask call is made by the client to submit a SCSIParallelTask for execution.

# Document: FilterInterruptRequest

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809938-filterinterruptrequest
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809938-filterinterruptrequest
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# FilterInterruptRequest

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Filter method called at primary interrupt time.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool FilterInterruptRequest (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

True if the hardware interrupt line should be disabled, otherwise false.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Filter method called at primary interrupt time. This should only be overridden by the child class in order to determine if an interrupt occurred for this controller instance. Since all work occurs at primary interrupt time, this routine should be quick and efficient and defer as much processing as possible to the HandleInterruptRequest() method.

NOTE: Unlike the HandleInterruptRequest() and HandleTimeout() methods, FilterInterruptRequest() is NOT called with the workloop lock held.

If the value returned by FilterInterruptRequest() is true, the secondary interrupt thread will be scheduled and the hardware interrupt line will be disabled. If the controller instance shares that interrupt line with other devices, it can cause large interrupt latencies. If the controller instance can disable the interrupt in the chip itself, the following can be done to reduce interrupt latencies:

\- Interrupt occurs - FilterInterruptRequest() method is called. - If the interrupt is not for this controller, return false immediately. - If the interrupt is for this controller, and the controller can disable interrupts for this chip, the controller should disable the interrupts for this chip, call SignalInterrupt(), and return false. This causes the secondary interrupt thread to get scheduled, yet does not disable the interrupt line for all devices tied to that interrupt. This effectively allows other devices to process their interrrupts, thus reducing interrupt latency for those devices. - HandleInterruptRequest() method is called. - Controller processes interrupt and completes I/O requests. - Controller re-enables interrupts for the device.

NOTE: If you use this approach, the interrupting condition MUST be cleared from the hardware, otherwise an infinite process interrupt loop will occur.

If the controller cannot disable interrupts on the chip, it should simply return true if an interrupt has occurred for its device.

# Document: FindTaskForAddress

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809945-findtaskforaddress
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809945-findtaskforaddress
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# FindTaskForAddress

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Find a task for a given Task Address, if one exists.

## Declaration

```objectivec
SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier FindTaskForAddress ( 
 SCSIDeviceIdentifiertheT, 
 SCSILogicalUnitNumbertheL, 
 SCSITaggedTaskIdentifiertheQ ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theT`: is the Target component of the I_T_L or I_T_L_Q nexus.
- `theL`: is the Logical Unit component of the I_T_L or I_T_L_Q nexus.
- `theQ`: is the Queue Tag component of the I_T_L_Q nexus. If this is an I_T_L nexus, then the kSCSIUntaggedTaskIdentifier constant should be used for theQ.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns a valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier or NULL if none found.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

If a valid Tagged Task Identifier is specified, this method will return the task specified by the Tagged Task Address if one is found, or else NULL will be returned. If zero is used as the Tagged Task Identifier, then this routine will search for an outstanding task based on the Untagged Task Address and return the task or else, if one is not found, return NULL.

# FindTaskForControllerIdentifier

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Find a task for a given Target and Controller Task Identifier

## Declaration

```objectivec
SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier FindTaskForControllerIdentifier ( 
 SCSIDeviceIdentifiertheTarget, 
 UInt64theIdentifier ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theTarget`: is the Target that the task .
- `theIdentifier`: is the controller task identifier set using the SCSI Parallel Task's SetControllerTaskIdentifier() method.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns a valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier or NULL if none found.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Allows the controller child class to find an outstanding task for a specified target and controller task identifier

# FreeSCSIParallelTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to allow the client to release a SCSIParallelTask

## Declaration

```objectivec
void FreeSCSIParallelTask (
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierreturnTask ); 
```

## Parameters

- `returnTask`: is a reference to the SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier to be returned.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The FreeSCSIParallelTask method is called by the client when a SCSIParallelTask has been completed and the associated returnTask needs to be returned to the pool.

# GetAutoSenseData

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to retrieve auto sense data buffer associated with a request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool GetAutoSenseData ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier parallelTask, 
 SCSI_Sense_Data *receivingBuffer, 
 UInt8 senseDataSize ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `receivingBuffer`: pointer to auto sense data buffer

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns true if successfully copied data into receivingBuffer

## See Also

# Document: GetCommandDescriptorBlock

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809978-getcommanddescriptorblock
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1809978-getcommanddescriptorblock
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetCommandDescriptorBlock

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to retrieve the SCSI Command Descriptor Block (CDB).

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool GetCommandDescriptorBlock ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask, 
 SCSICommandDescriptorBlock *cdbData ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `cdbData`: is a SCSICommandDescriptorBlock pointer to 16 byte CDB

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns true if data was copied to cdbData pointer

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This will always return a 16 Byte CDB. If the Protocol Layer driver does not support 16 Byte CDBs, it will have to create a local SCSICommandDescriptorBlock variable to get the CDB data and then transfer the needed bytes from there.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetDMACommand

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to retrieve a pointer to an IODMACommand from the request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IODMACommand * GetDMACommand ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns pointer to an IODMACommand which is used in conjunction with the task.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For devices utilizing DMA, the IODMACommand object should be obtained via GetDMACommand(). The subclass is responsible for calling prepare() on the IODMACommand object using the proper offset obtained via GetDataBufferOffset() and correct size obtained via GetRequestedDataTransferCount(). The subclass is further responsible for calling complete() on the IODMACommand object once all DMA operations have finished. NB: Subclasses should not call IODMACommand::setMemoryDescriptor().

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetSCSIParallelFeatureNegotiationCount

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to retrieve the number of requested negotiations.

## Declaration

```objectivec
UInt64 GetSCSIParallelFeatureNegotiationCount ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

an unsigned integer up to 64 bits in size.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Query as to the number of SCSI Parallel Features that are requested to either be negotitated or cleared. These are all features that are set to either kSCSIParallelFeature_AttemptNegotiation or kSCSIParallelFeature_ClearNegotiation. If the return value is zero, then all features are set to kSCSIParallelFeature_NoNegotiation and all feature negotiations are to remain as they currently exist.

## Overview

These are all features that are set to either kSCSIParallelFeature_NegotitiationCleared or kSCSIParallelFeature_NegotitiationSuccess. If the return value is zero, then all features are set to kSCSIParallelFeature_NegotitiationUnchanged.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetSCSIParallelTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to allow the client to get a SCSIParallelTask

## Declaration

```objectivec
SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier GetSCSIParallelTask (
 boolblockForCommand ); 
```

## Parameters

- `blockForCommand`: If the blockForCommand parameter is set to false and there are no free SCSIParallelTasks, this method will return NULL, otherwise it will wait for one to become available before returning.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

If there is a SCSI Parallel Task available, a reference to it will be returned.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Get a SCSIParallelTask from the controller so that a request can be issued to the HBA driver.

# Document: GetTimeoutDuration

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810247-gettimeoutduration
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810247-gettimeoutduration
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetTimeoutDuration

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to retrieve the timeout duration in milliseconds for a request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
UInt32 GetTimeoutDuration (
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns timeout duration in milliseconds

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Method to retrieve the timeout duration in milliseconds for a request. A value of zero represents an infinite timeout, or on hardware where infinite timeouts are not possible, substitute the longest timeout possible.

# HandleInterruptRequest

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Handle Interrupt Request

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandleInterruptRequest (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The HandleInterruptRequest is used to notify an HBA specific subclass that an interrupt request needs to be serviced. It is called on the workloop (it holds the gate) at secondary interrupt level.

# HandleTimeout

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to handle command timeouts.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandleTimeout ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelRequest ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelRequest`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Method to handle command timeouts. This should be overridden by the child class in order to clean up HBA specific structures after a timeout has occurred. This method is called on the workloop (it holds the gate).

# Document: IncrementRealizedDataTransferCount

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810290-incrementrealizeddatatransfercou

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# IncrementRealizedDataTransferCount

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Increments the realized data transfer count. This method is helpful for when the HBA has to do multiple passes of DMA because there are more scatter-gather elements than it can process in one pass.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void IncrementRealizedDataTransferCount ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask, 
 UInt64realizedTransferCountInBytes ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `realizedTransferCountInBytes`: is the number of bytes to add to the realized data count for the task.

# Document: InitializeController

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810299-initializecontroller
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810299-initializecontroller
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# InitializeController

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to initialize the controller

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool InitializeController (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

return true means that initialization was successful.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

It is guaranteed that the InitializeController() will only be called once per instantiation. The InitializeController() methods allows the subclass driver to do all the necessary initialization required by the hardware before it is able to accept requests to execute. All necessary allocation of resources should be made during this method call. This is the first method that will be called in the subclass.

```objectivec
virtual bool InitializeDMASpecification (
 IODMACommand *command ); 
```

## Parameters

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# InitializeTargetForID

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to initialize a target device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool InitializeTargetForID ( 
 SCSITargetIdentifier targetID ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns true if the target was successfully initialized.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method will be called to initialize a target device in a single-threaded manner. The HBA can use this method to probe the target or do anything else necessary before the device object is registered with IOKit for matching.

# NotifyClientsOfPortStatusChange

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method called to notify clients of port status change events.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void NotifyClientsOfPortStatusChange (
 SCSIPortStatus newStatus ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is used by the HBA child class to inform the parent class and any clients that a port has changed status.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# ProcessParallelTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called by client to process a parallel task.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SCSIServiceResponse ProcessParallelTask ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelRequest ) = 0; 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelRequest`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

serviceResponse (see \<IOKit/scsi/SCSITask.h\>)

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called to process a parallel task (i.e. put the command on the bus). The HBA specific sublcass must implement this method.

# RemoveHBAProperty

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor for removing a property for this object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void RemoveHBAProperty (
 const char *key ); 
```

## Parameters

- `key`: A pointer to a valid OSString object which represents the key. See the SetHBAProperty() method for a list of valid keys.

## See Also

### Miscellaneous

- [CompleteParallelTask](1809862-completeparalleltask.md): Parallel Task Completion

# RemoveTargetProperty

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor for removing a property from a specific target.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void RemoveTargetProperty (
 SCSIDeviceIdentifierdevice, 
 const char *key ); 
```

## Parameters

- `device`: A pointer to a valid IOSCSIParallelInterfaceDevice.
- `key`: A pointer to a valid OSString object which represents the key.

# Document: ReportHBAConstraints

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810388-reporthbaconstraints
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810388-reporthbaconstraints
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# ReportHBAConstraints

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to report the I/O constraints for this controller. A list of valid keys includes: kIOMaximumSegmentCountReadKey, (required) kIOMaximumSegmentCountWriteKey, (required) kIOMaximumSegmentByteCountReadKey, (required) kIOMaximumSegmentByteCountWriteKey, (required) kIOMinimumSegmentAlignmentByteCountKey, (required) kIOMaximumSegmentAddressableBitCountKey, (required) kIOMinimumHBADataAlignmentMaskKey (required) kIOHierarchicalLogicalUnitSupportKey (optional). NB: These keys and their values are described in this header and \<IOKit/IOKitKeys.h\>

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void ReportHBAConstraints (
 OSDictionary *constraints. ); 
```

## Parameters

- `constraints.`: An OSDictionary object used to aggregate the key/value pairs. Subclasses must set the required keys if they override this method. If a subclass does not provide the required keys, the system will panic.

```objectivec
virtual SCSILogicalUnitNumber ReportHBAHighestLogicalUnitNumber (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

This method is used to query the HBA child class to determine what the highest Logical Unit Number that the controller can address.

# ReportHighestSupportedDeviceID

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Get the highest supported SCSI Device Identifier.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SCSIDeviceIdentifier ReportHighestSupportedDeviceID (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns highest SCSIDeviceIdentifier

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method will be called to determine the value of the highest SCSI Device Identifier supported by the HBA. This value will be used to determine the last ID to process.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# ReportMaximumTaskCount

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Report Maximum Task Count

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual UInt32 ReportMaximumTaskCount (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns maximum (non-zero) task count.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method will be called to retrieve the maximum number of outstanding tasks the HBA can process. This number must be greater than zero or the controller driver will fail to match and load.

# SetAutoSenseData

**Interface language:** Objective-C

Method to set the auto sense data buffer associated with a request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool SetAutoSenseData ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier parallelTask, 
 SCSI_Sense_Data *newSenseData, 
 UInt8 senseDataSize ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `newSensedata`: pointer to auto sense data buffer

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns true if data in newSenseData was succesfully into the task object

# Document: SetControllerTaskIdentifier

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810503-setcontrollertaskidentifier
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810503-setcontrollertaskidentifier
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# SetControllerTaskIdentifier

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to set the Controller Task Identifier.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void SetControllerTaskIdentifier ( 
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifierparallelTask, 
 UInt64newIdentifier ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `newIdentifier`: unsigned 64 bit integer token.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

none

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method allows the Controller Child Class driver to set a unique identifier to associate with the specified SCSI Parallel Task. This identifier is designed to be used by controllers that do not have access to the LUN and Tag information when notified by the HBA that a request has completed. If the kSCSIParallelTaskControllerIDQueueHead is used, this member routine will return the first Task on the queue.

# Document: SetHBAProperty

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810516-sethbaproperty
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810516-sethbaproperty
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# SetHBAProperty

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor for setting a property for this object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool SetHBAProperty (
 const char *key, 
 OSObject *value ); 
```

## Parameters

- `key`: A pointer to a valid OSString object which represents the key. A list of valid keys includes: kIOPropertyVendorNameKey, kIOPropertyProductNameKey, kIOPropertyProductRevisionLevelKey, kIOPropertyPortDescriptionKey, kIOPropertyPortSpeedKey, kIOPropertyPortTopologyKey, kIOPropertySCSIParallelSignalingTypeKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelCableDescriptionKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelNodeWorldWideNameKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelPortWorldWideNameKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelAddressIdentifierKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelALPAKey, and kIOPropertySASAddressKey. NB: These keys and their values are described in \<IOKit/storage/IOStorageDeviceCharacteristics.h\> and \<IOKit/storage/IOStorageProtocolCharacteristics.h\>
- `value`: Pointer to an OSObject (one of type OSData, OSString, etc.) which represents the value for the property. The value must be of the proper type, and/or size for the specified key.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns true if identifier was properly set, otherwise false.

# Document: SetTargetProperty

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810557-settargetproperty
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810557-settargetproperty
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# SetTargetProperty

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor for setting a property for a specific target.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool SetTargetProperty (
 SCSIDeviceIdentifierdevice, 
 const char *key, 
 OSObject *value ); 
```

## Parameters

- `device`: A pointer to a valid IOSCSIParallelInterfaceDevice.
- `key`: A pointer to a valid OSString object which represents the key. A list of valid keys includes: kIOPropertySASAddressKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelNodeWorldWideNameKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelPortWorldWideNameKey, kIOPropertyFibreChannelAddressIdentifierKey, and kIOPropertyFibreChannelALPAKey. NB: These keys and their values are described in \<IOKit/storage/IOStorageProtocolCharacteristics.h\>
- `value`: Pointer to an OSObject (one of type OSData, OSString, etc.) which represents the value for the property. The value must be of the proper type and size for the specified key.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

returns true if identifier was properly set, otherwise false.

# SetTimeoutForTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method to set the timeout duration in milliseconds for a request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void SetTimeoutForTask (
 SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier parallelTask, 
 UInt32 timeoutOverride = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `parallelTask`: A valid SCSIParallelTaskIdentifier.
- `timeoutOverride`: A timeout value in milliseconds in case the HBA driver wishes to override the default value provided in the parallelTask.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Method to set the timeout duration in milliseconds for a request.

# Document: SignalInterrupt

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810589-signalinterrupt
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810589-signalinterrupt
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# SignalInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Signals that an interrupt has occurred.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void SignalInterrupt (
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Subclasses of IOSCSIParallelInterfaceController should call this method in order to get the secondary interrupt thread scheduled if and only if they will be returning false from their overriden FilterInterruptRequest() method. See the discussion for the FilterInterruptRequest() method for more details.

NOTE: This method should only be called from within the FilterInterruptRequest() method and at no other time.

Available in 10.3.3 or later.

# StartController

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to start the controller

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool StartController (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

return true means that start was successful.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The StartController will always be called before any requests are sent to the driver for execution. This method is called after an initialize to start the services provided by the specific HBA driver or called after a StopController call to restart those services. After this call completes, all services provided by the HBA driver are available to the client.

Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810629-stopcontroller
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# StopController

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to stop the controller

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void StopController (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The StopController method will be called any time that the system wants the card to stop accepting requests. ( See StartController discussion ). The subclass should disable the hardware interrupt for the particular controller (if possible) in this method.

# Document: SuspendServices

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810641-suspendservices
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810641-suspendservices
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# SuspendServices

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to suspend controller services

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void SuspendServices (
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Method will be called when the system wants to suspend the services that are provided by the HBA driver. This call is not a reset and the driver shall retain all state data between this so that if a ResumeServices call is received, the driver can continue providing services without a visible difference to the client. The driver may receive multiple SuspendServices calls without receiving a ResumeServices call and should ignore any after the first until a ResumeServices call is received.

# Document: TerminateController

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810669-terminatecontroller
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiparallelinterfacecontroller/1810669-terminatecontroller
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# TerminateController

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called to terminate the controller

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void TerminateController (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

It is guaranteed that the TerminateController() will only be called once and only after the InitializeController() method and only if true was returned in response to the InitializeController() method. The TerminateController() method allows the subclass to release all resources that were acquired for operation of the hardware and shutdown all hardware services. This is the last method of the subclass that will be called before the class is destroyed.

- [IOSCSIProtocolServices](ioscsiprotocolservices.md): This class defines the public SCSI Protocol Services Layer API for any class that implements SCSI protocol services. A protocol services layer driver is responsible for taking incoming SCSITaskIdentifier objects and translating them to the native command type for the native protocol interface (e.g. SBP-2 ORB on FireWire).
- [IOSCSIProtocolInterface](ioscsiprotocolinterface.md): This class defines the public SCSI Protocol Layer API for any class that provides Protocol services or needs to provide the Protocol Service API for passing service requests to a Protocol Service driver.

# Document: IOSCSIProtocolInterface

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolinterface
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolinterface
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# IOSCSIProtocolInterface

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Class  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

This class defines the public SCSI Protocol Layer API for any class that provides Protocol services or needs to provide the Protocol Service API for passing service requests to a Protocol Service driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
class IOSCSIProtocolInterface : IOService
```

## Topics

### Miscellaneous

- [AbortCommand](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810020-abortcommand.md): Obsolete. Do not use this method.
- [AbortTask](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810034-aborttask.md): Aborts a task based on the Logical Unit and tagged task identifier.
- [AbortTaskSet](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810053-aborttaskset.md): Aborts a task set based on the Logical Unit.
- [CheckPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810067-checkpowerstate.md): Called by clients to ensure device is in correct power state before issuing I/O.
- [ClearACA](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810087-clearaca.md): Clears an Auto-Contingent Allegiance (ACA) for the specified Logical Unit.
- [ClearTaskSet](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810108-cleartaskset.md): Clears a task set for the specified Logical Unit.
- [ExecuteCommand](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810126-executecommand.md): Called to send a SCSITask and transport it across the physical wire(s) to the device.
- [finalize](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810146-finalize.md): Finalizes the destruction of an IOService object.
- [free](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810163-free.md): Called to release all resources held by the object.
- [GetCommandGate](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810184-getcommandgate.md): Accessor method to obtain the IOCommandGate.
- [GetInitialPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810205-getinitialpowerstate.md): This method is called to obtain the initial power state of the device (usually the highest).
- [GetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810233-getuserclientexclusivitystate.md): Gets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [HandleCheckPowerState()](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810265-handlecheckpowerstate.md): The HandleCheckPowerState (void) method is on the serialized side of the command gate and can change member variables safely without multi-threading issues. It's main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state the class registered with.
- [HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32)](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810294-handlecheckpowerstate.md): The HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is called by the subclasses and is passed the maxPowerState number given to the power manager at initialization time. This guarantees the threads block until that power state has been achieved.
- [HandleCheckPowerState(void)](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810368-handlecheckpowerstate.md): The HandleCheckPowerState (void) method is on the serialized side of the command gate and can change member variables safely without multi-threading issues. It's main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state the class registered with.
- [HandleGetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810391-handlegetuserclientexclusivityst.md): Gets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [HandlePowerChange](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810424-handlepowerchange.md): The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.
- [HandleProtocolServiceFeature](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810462-handleprotocolservicefeature.md): This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature.
- [HandleSetPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810510-handlesetpowerstate.md): The HandleSetPowerState method is called by the glue code and is on the serialized side of the command gate.
- [HandleSetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810570-handlesetuserclientexclusivityst.md): Sets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [InitializePowerManagement](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810624-initializepowermanagement.md): This method is called to initialize power management.
- [initialPowerStateForDomainState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810676-initialpowerstatefordomainstate.md): Determines which power state a device is in, given the current power domain state.
- [IsPowerManagementIntialized](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810727-ispowermanagementintialized.md): Called to determine if power management is initialized.
- [IsProtocolServiceSupported](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810761-isprotocolservicesupported.md): This method is called to query for support of a protocol specific service feature.
- [LogicalUnitReset](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810795-logicalunitreset.md): Resets the specified Logical Unit.
- [setPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810826-setpowerstate.md): Requests a power managed driver to change the power state of its device.
- [SetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810852-setuserclientexclusivitystate.md): Sets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [sGetPowerTransistionInProgress](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810884-sgetpowertransistioninprogress.md): The sGetPowerTransistionInProgress method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sGetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810914-sgetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sGetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleCheckPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810945-shandlecheckpowerstate.md): The sHandleCheckPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleSetPowerState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810965-shandlesetpowerstate.md): The sHandleSetPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sPowerManagement](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810988-spowermanagement.md): The sPowerManagement method is a static C-function which is called using mach's thread_call API. It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.
- [sSetUserClientExclusivityState](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811011-ssetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [start](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811044-start.md): During an IOService object's instantiation, starts the IOService object that has been selected to run on the provider.
- [TargetReset](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811073-targetreset.md): Resets the target device.
- [TicklePowerManager()](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811095-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [TicklePowerManager(UInt32)](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811118-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).
- [TicklePowerManager(void)](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811187-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [willTerminate](ioscsiprotocolinterface/1811210-willterminate.md): Passes a termination up the stack.

It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.
- [sSetUserClientExclusivityState](1811011-ssetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.

- [TargetReset](1811073-targetreset.md): Resets the target device.
- [TicklePowerManager()](1811095-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [TicklePowerManager(UInt32)](1811118-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).
- [TicklePowerManager(void)](1811187-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.

# AbortTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Aborts a task based on the Logical Unit and tagged task identifier.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SCSIServiceResponse AbortTask (
 UInt8theLogicalUnit,
 SCSITaggedTaskIdentifiertheTag ) = 0; 
```

## Parameters

- `theLogicalUnit`: This value should be zero unless the device driver is more complex and managing multiple Logical Units.
- `theTag`: A valid SCSITaggedTaskIdentifier representing an outstanding SCSITask.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A valid SCSIServiceResponse code.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Aborts a task based on the Logical Unit and tagged task identifier. Subclasses must override this method. Third party subclasses should not need to override this method.

# Document: CheckPowerState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810067-checkpowerstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolinterface/1810067-checkpowerstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# CheckPowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Called by clients to ensure device is in correct power state before issuing I/O.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void CheckPowerState (
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Called by clients to ensure device is in correct power state before issuing I/O. If the device is not ready to handle such requests, it gives the driver a chance to block the thread until the device is ready. Subclasses should not need to override this method.

## See Also

### Miscellaneous

- [AbortCommand](1810020-abortcommand.md): Obsolete. Do not use this method.
- [AbortTask](1810034-aborttask.md): Aborts a task based on the Logical Unit and tagged task identifier.
- [AbortTaskSet](1810053-aborttaskset.md): Aborts a task set based on the Logical Unit.
- [ClearACA](1810087-clearaca.md): Clears an Auto-Contingent Allegiance (ACA) for the specified Logical Unit.
- [ClearTaskSet](1810108-cleartaskset.md): Clears a task set for the specified Logical Unit.
- [ExecuteCommand](1810126-executecommand.md): Called to send a SCSITask and transport it across the physical wire(s) to the device.

It's main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state the class registered with.
- [HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32)](1810294-handlecheckpowerstate.md): The HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is called by the subclasses and is passed the maxPowerState number given to the power manager at initialization time. This guarantees the threads block until that power state has been achieved.

- [HandlePowerChange](1810424-handlepowerchange.md): The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.
- [HandleProtocolServiceFeature](1810462-handleprotocolservicefeature.md): This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature.

- [sHandleSetPowerState](1810965-shandlesetpowerstate.md): The sHandleSetPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.

It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.
- [sSetUserClientExclusivityState](1811011-ssetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.

- [TargetReset](1811073-targetreset.md): Resets the target device.
- [TicklePowerManager()](1811095-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [TicklePowerManager(UInt32)](1811118-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetUserClientExclusivityState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Gets the current exclusivity state of the user client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool GetUserClientExclusivityState (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if a user client is in exclusive control of the device, `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The GetUserClientExclusivityState() method is called by the SCSITaskUserClient to determine if any user client is holding exclusive access at the current time. This is simply a preflight check and a return value of `false` does not guarantee that a subsequent call to SetUserClientExclusivityState() will return successfully.

# HandleCheckPowerState()

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The HandleCheckPowerState (void) method is on the serialized side of the command gate and can change member variables safely without multi-threading issues. It's main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state the class registered with.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandleCheckPowerState (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The HandleCheckPowerState (void) method is on the serialized side of the command gate and can change member variables safely without multi-threading issues. It's main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state the class registered with. Subclasses must override this method. Third party subclasses shouldn't need to override this method but can to alter the default behavior.

# HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The HandleCheckPowerState(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is called by the subclasses and is passed the maxPowerState number given to the power manager at initialization time. This guarantees the threads block until that power state has been achieved.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void HandleCheckPowerState (
 UInt32maxPowerState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `maxPowerState`: The maximum power state in the power state array.

virtual bool HandleGetUserClientExclusivityState (

## Return Value

`true` if a user client is in exclusive control of the device, `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

# HandlePowerChange

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandlePowerChange (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls. Subclasses must override this method. Third party subclasses shouldn't need to override this method but can to alter the default behavior.

# HandleProtocolServiceFeature

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool HandleProtocolServiceFeature ( 
 SCSIProtocolFeaturefeature, 
 void *serviceValue ) = 0; 
```

## Parameters

- `feature`: A valid SCSIProtocolFeature. See enums for SCSIProtocolFeature.
- `serviceValue`: A pointer to a structure/value that is used in conjunction with the feature requested. See enums for SCSIProtocolFeature. NB: This parameter may be NULL for certain feature requests.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the service feature request succeeded, `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature. Subclasses of IOSCSIProtocolServices should override this method.

- [HandleGetUserClientExclusivityState](1810391-handlegetuserclientexclusivityst.md): Gets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [HandlePowerChange](1810424-handlepowerchange.md): The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.
- [HandleProtocolServiceFeature](1810462-handleprotocolservicefeature.md): This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature.
- [HandleSetPowerState](1810510-handlesetpowerstate.md): The HandleSetPowerState method is called by the glue code and is on the serialized side of the command gate.

- [IsProtocolServiceSupported](1810761-isprotocolservicesupported.md): This method is called to query for support of a protocol specific service feature.
- [LogicalUnitReset](1810795-logicalunitreset.md): Resets the specified Logical Unit.
- [setPowerState](1810826-setpowerstate.md): Requests a power managed driver to change the power state of its device.

- [sGetUserClientExclusivityState](1810914-sgetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sGetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleCheckPowerState](1810945-shandlecheckpowerstate.md): The sHandleCheckPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleSetPowerState](1810965-shandlesetpowerstate.md): The sHandleSetPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sPowerManagement](1810988-spowermanagement.md): The sPowerManagement method is a static C-function which is called using mach's thread_call API. It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.
- [sSetUserClientExclusivityState](1811011-ssetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.

- [TargetReset](1811073-targetreset.md): Resets the target device.
- [TicklePowerManager()](1811095-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [TicklePowerManager(UInt32)](1811118-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. # InitializePowerManagement

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

This method is called to initialize power management.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void InitializePowerManagement (
 IOService *provider ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The power management provider (i.e. the provider to attach to in the PowerManagement tree). This may be a device that is not in the PM Tree itself, in which case, the IOService plane is traversed towards the root node in an effort to find a node in the PM Tree.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called to initialize power management. It will call PMinit(), joinPMTree(), and makeUsable(). This method does not call registerPowerDriver(). Subclasses may override this method to change the behavior (such as the number of power states).

# initialPowerStateForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines which power state a device is in, given the current power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long initialPowerStateForDomainState (
 IOPMPowerFlagsflags ); 
```

## Parameters

- `flags`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls this method once, when the driver is initializing power management. Subclasses should not need to override this method.

# IsProtocolServiceSupported

**Interface language:** Objective-C

This method is called to query for support of a protocol specific service feature.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool IsProtocolServiceSupported ( 
 SCSIProtocolFeaturefeature,

```

## Parameters

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the feature is supported, `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

- [HandlePowerChange](1810424-handlepowerchange.md): The HandlePowerChange method is pure virtual and is left to each protocol or application layer driver to implement. It is guaranteed to be called on its own thread of execution and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.
- [HandleProtocolServiceFeature](1810462-handleprotocolservicefeature.md): This method is called to enact support of a protocol specific service feature.
- [HandleSetPowerState](1810510-handlesetpowerstate.md): The HandleSetPowerState method is called by the glue code and is on the serialized side of the command gate.
- [HandleSetUserClientExclusivityState](1810570-handlesetuserclientexclusivityst.md): Sets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [InitializePowerManagement](1810624-initializepowermanagement.md): This method is called to initialize power management.
- [initialPowerStateForDomainState](1810676-initialpowerstatefordomainstate.md): Determines which power state a device is in, given the current power domain state.
- [IsPowerManagementIntialized](1810727-ispowermanagementintialized.md): Called to determine if power management is initialized.
- [LogicalUnitReset](1810795-logicalunitreset.md): Resets the specified Logical Unit.
- [setPowerState](1810826-setpowerstate.md): Requests a power managed driver to change the power state of its device.
- [SetUserClientExclusivityState](1810852-setuserclientexclusivitystate.md): Sets the current exclusivity state of the user client.
- [sGetPowerTransistionInProgress](1810884-sgetpowertransistioninprogress.md): The sGetPowerTransistionInProgress method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sGetUserClientExclusivityState](1810914-sgetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sGetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleCheckPowerState](1810945-shandlecheckpowerstate.md): The sHandleCheckPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sHandleSetPowerState](1810965-shandlesetpowerstate.md): The sHandleSetPowerState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [sPowerManagement](1810988-spowermanagement.md): The sPowerManagement method is a static C-function which is called using mach's thread_call API. It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.
- [sSetUserClientExclusivityState](1811011-ssetuserclientexclusivitystate.md): The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.
- [start](1811044-start.md): During an IOService object's instantiation, starts the IOService object that has been selected to run on the provider.
- [TargetReset](1811073-targetreset.md): Resets the target device.
- [TicklePowerManager()](1811095-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [TicklePowerManager(UInt32)](1811118-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).
- [TicklePowerManager(void)](1811187-ticklepowermanager.md): The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.
- [willTerminate](1811210-willterminate.md): Passes a termination up the stack.

# setPowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests a power managed driver to change the power state of its device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn setPowerState (
 unsigned longpowerStateOrdinal,
 IOService *whichDevice ); 
```

## Parameters

- `powerStateOrdinal`: The number in the power state array to which the drive is being instructed to change.
- `whichDevice`: A pointer to the power management object which registered to manage power for this device. The whichDevice field is not pertinent to us since the driver is both the "policy maker" for the device, and the "policy implementor" for the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

See IOService.h for details.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Requests a power managed driver to change the power state of its device. Most subclasses of IOSCSIProtocolInterface have class-specific mechanisms and should not override this routine. See IOSCSIProtocolServices.h, IOSCSIBlockCommandsDevice.h, IOSCSIReducedBlockCommandsDevice.h, and IOSCSIMultimediaCommandsDevice.h for more information about power management changes. Subclasses should not need to override this method.

# SetUserClientExclusivityState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sets the current exclusivity state of the user client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn SetUserClientExclusivityState (
 IOService *userClient,
 boolstate ); 
```

## Parameters

The SetUserClientExclusivityState() method is called by the SCSITaskUserClient to set the exclusive access mode.

# sPowerManagement

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The sPowerManagement method is a static C-function which is called using mach's thread_call API. It guarantees us a thread of execution which is different than the power management thread and the workloop thread on which we can issue commands to the device synchronously or asynchronously without worrying about deadlocks. It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.

It calls through to HandlePowerChange, which is a state machine used to direct power management.

The sSetUserClientExclusivityState method is a static function used as C-\>C++ glue for going behind the command gate.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static void sSetUserClientExclusivityState (
 IOSCSIProtocolInterface *self,
 IOReturn *result,
 IOService *userClient,
 boolstate ); 
```

## Parameters

# TicklePowerManager()

# TicklePowerManager(UInt32)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager (void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool TicklePowerManager (
 UInt32maxPowerState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `maxPowerState`: The maximum power state in the power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The result of the call to activityTickle(). See IOService.h for details.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The TicklePowerManager(UInt32 maxPowerState) method is a convenience function which can be called by subclasses in TicklePowerManager(void) in order to tell the power manager to reset idle timer or bring the device into the requested state. It returns whatever is returned by activityTickle (true if device is in the requested state, false if it is not).

# TicklePowerManager(void)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void TicklePowerManager (
 void ) = 0; 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The TicklePowerManager(void) method is called by CheckPowerState and sends an activity tickle to the power manager so that the idle timer is reset. Subclasses must override this method. Third party subclasses shouldn't need to override this method but can to alter the default behavior.

# willTerminate

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Passes a termination up the stack.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool willTerminate (
 IOService *provider,
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The terminated provider of this object.
- `options`: Options originally passed to terminate().

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Notification that a provider has been terminated, sent before recursing up the stack, in root-to-leaf order.

# IOSCSIProtocolServices

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Class  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

This class defines the public SCSI Protocol Services Layer API for any class that implements SCSI protocol services. A protocol services layer driver is responsible for taking incoming SCSITaskIdentifier objects and translating them to the native command type for the native protocol interface (e.g. SBP-2 ORB on FireWire).

## Declaration

```objectivec
class IOSCSIProtocolServices : IOSCSIProtocolInterface
```

## Topics

### Miscellaneous

- [AbortCommand](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809724-abortcommand.md): Deprecated. Do not use.
- [AbortSCSICommand](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809736-abortscsicommand.md): Pure virtual method subclasses must implement so that SCSITasks may be aborted.
- [AbortSCSITaskFromQueue](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809747-abortscsitaskfromqueue.md): Deprecated internal method.
- [AbortTask](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809759-aborttask.md): The Task Management function to allow the SCSI Application Layer client to request that a specific task be aborted.
- [AbortTaskSet](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809765-aborttaskset.md): The Task Management function to allow the SCSI Application Layer client to request that a complete task set be aborted.
- [AddSCSITaskToHeadOfQueue](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809777-addscsitasktoheadofqueue.md): Internal method called to add a SCSITask to the head of the processing queue.
- [AddSCSITaskToQueue](ioscsiprotocolservices/1809791-addscsitasktoqueue.md): Internal method called to add a SCSITask to the processing queue.

## Overview

Deprecated. Do not use.

## See Also

### Miscellaneous

- [AbortSCSICommand](1809736-abortscsicommand.md): Pure virtual method subclasses must implement so that SCSITasks may be aborted.
- [AbortSCSITaskFromQueue](1809747-abortscsitaskfromqueue.md): Deprecated internal method.
- [AbortTask](1809759-aborttask.md): The Task Management function to allow the SCSI Application Layer client to request that a specific task be aborted.
- [AbortTaskSet](1809765-aborttaskset.md): The Task Management function to allow the SCSI Application Layer client to request that a complete task set be aborted.
- [AddSCSITaskToHeadOfQueue](1809777-addscsitasktoheadofqueue.md): Internal method called to add a SCSITask to the head of the processing queue.
- [AddSCSITaskToQueue](1809791-addscsitasktoqueue.md): Internal method called to add a SCSITask to the processing queue.
- [ClearACA](1809805-clearaca.md): The Task Management function to clear an Auto-Contingent Allegiance condition.
- [ClearTaskSet](1809813-cleartaskset.md): The Task Management function to clear a task set.
- [CommandCompleted](1809823-commandcompleted.md): Method subclass calls to complete a SCSITask.
- [CreateSCSITargetDevice](1809830-createscsitargetdevice.md): Used to create a SCSITargetDevice which will manage logical units.
- [EnsureAutosenseDescriptorExists](1809843-ensureautosensedescriptorexists.md): Internal method, not to be called by subclasses.
- [ExecuteCommand](1809854-executecommand.md): ExecuteCommand method will take a SCSI Task and transport it across the physical wire(s) to the device.
- [free](1809869-free.md): Frees data structures that were allocated during start().
- [GetAutosenseRequestedDataTransferCount](1809881-getautosenserequesteddatatransfe.md): Accessor method to retrieve the requested data transfer count for autosense data associated with the specified request.
- [GetCommandDescriptorBlock](1809892-getcommanddescriptorblock.md): Accessor method to retrieve the Command Descriptor Block associated with the specified request.
- [GetCommandDescriptorBlockSize](1809902-getcommanddescriptorblocksize.md): Accessor method to retrieve the Command Descriptor Block size associated with the specified request.
- [GetDataBuffer](1809915-getdatabuffer.md): Accessor method to retrieve the data buffer associated with the specified request.
- [GetDataBufferOffset](1809935-getdatabufferoffset.md): Accessor method to retrieve the data buffer offset associated with the specified request.
- [GetDataTransferDirection](1809946-getdatatransferdirection.md): Accessor method to retrieve the data transfer direction associated with the specified request.
- [GetInitialPowerState](1809959-getinitialpowerstate.md): This method is called once, right after InitializePowerManagement() in order to determine what state the device is initially in at startup time (usually the highest power mode).
- [GetLogicalUnitBytes](1809964-getlogicalunitbytes.md): Accessor method to retrieve the logical unit bytes associated with the specified request.
- [GetLogicalUnitNumber](1809972-getlogicalunitnumber.md): Accessor method to retrieve the logical unit number associated with the specified request.
- [GetProtocolLayerReference](1809980-getprotocollayerreference.md): Accessor method to retrieve the protocol layer reference.
- [GetRealizedDataTransferCount](1809989-getrealizeddatatransfercount.md): Accessor method to retrieve the realized data transfer count associated with the specified request.
- [GetRequestedDataTransferCount](1809996-getrequesteddatatransfercount.md): Accessor method to retrieve the requested data transfer count associated with the specified request.
- [GetTaskAttribute](1810005-gettaskattribute.md): Accessor method to retrieve the SCSITaskAttribute associated with the specified request.
- [GetTaskExecutionMode](1810017-gettaskexecutionmode.md): Internal method used to retrieve the task execution mode.
- [GetTaskState](1810028-gettaskstate.md): Accessor method to retrieve the SCSITaskState associated with the specified request.
- [GetTimeoutDuration](1810038-gettimeoutduration.md): Accessor method to retrieve the timeout duration in milliseconds associated with the specified request.
- [HandleAbortTask](1810051-handleaborttask.md): HandleAbortTask instructs the Protocol Services driver to abort the task.
- [HandleAbortTaskSet](1810062-handleaborttaskset.md): HandleAbortTaskSet instructs the Protocol Services driver to abort the task set.
- [HandleCheckPowerState](1810080-handlecheckpowerstate.md): Method called to check if the device is in the correct power state for an I/O.
- [HandleClearACA](1810093-handleclearaca.md): HandleClearACA instructs the Protocol Services driver to clear an auto-contingent allegiance.
- [HandleClearTaskSet](1810105-handlecleartaskset.md): HandleClearTaskSet instructs the Protocol Services driver to clear the task set.
- [HandleLogicalUnitReset](1810119-handlelogicalunitreset.md): HandleLogicalUnitReset instructs the Protocol Services driver to reset the logical unit.
- [HandlePowerChange](1810127-handlepowerchange.md): This method is called to handle a power change.
- [HandlePowerOff](1810144-handlepoweroff.md): Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power off call (called on the way to sleep).
- [HandlePowerOn](1810154-handlepoweron.md): Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power on call (called on the way back up from sleep).
- [HandleProtocolServiceFeature](1810168-handleprotocolservicefeature.md): HandleProtocolServiceFeature instructs the Protocol Services driver to perform the necessary tasks for the indicated feature.
- [HandleTargetReset](1810176-handletargetreset.md): HandleTargetReset instructs the Protocol Services driver to reset the target.
- [init](1810187-init.md): Standard init method for all IORegistryEntry subclasses.
- [InitializePowerManagement](1810204-initializepowermanagement.md): Subclasses call this method to initialize power management.
- [IsProtocolServiceSupported](1810217-isprotocolservicesupported.md): IsProtocolServiceSupported will return true if the specified feature is supported by the protocol layer.
- [LogicalUnitReset](1810234-logicalunitreset.md): The Task Management function to reset a logical unit.
- [ProcessCompletedTask](1810248-processcompletedtask.md): Internal method called to process completed SCSITasks.
- [RegisterSCSITaskCompletionRoutine](1810264-registerscsitaskcompletionroutin.md): Used by IOSCSITargetDevice to register a completion routine.
- [RejectSCSITasksCurrentlyQueued](1810276-rejectscsitaskscurrentlyqueued.md): Internal method called to reject currently enqueued SCSITasks.

# AbortSCSICommand

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Pure virtual method subclasses must implement so that SCSITasks may be aborted.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SCSIServiceResponse AbortSCSICommand (
 SCSITaskIdentifierrequest ) = 0; 
```

## Parameters

- `request`: A valid SCSITaskIdentifier representing the command to be aborted.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A valid SCSIServiceResponse.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Provides the capability for a caller to request that a particular SCSITask be aborted.

# CommandCompleted

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method subclass calls to complete a SCSITask.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void CommandCompleted (
 SCSITaskIdentifierrequest, 
 SCSIServiceResponseserviceResponse, 
 SCSITaskStatustaskStatus ); 
```

## Parameters

- `request`: A valid SCSITaskIdentifier indicating the request to complete.
- `serviceResponse`: A valid SCSIServiceResponse value.
- `taskStatus`: A valid SCSITaskStatus value.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Subclasses will call this inherited method when the command executed by SendSCSICommand has completed.

# CreateSCSITargetDevice

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Used to create a SCSITargetDevice which will manage logical units.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool CreateSCSITargetDevice (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

True if successful, otherwise false.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The CreateSCSITargetDevice member routine will create the appropriate object to represent the Target portion of a SCSI Device. This object is responsible for managing the Target functions of the SCSI Device including the Task Manager and Logical Units.

# Document: GetCommandDescriptorBlock

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolservices/1809892-getcommanddescriptorblock
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolservices/1809892-getcommanddescriptorblock
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetCommandDescriptorBlock

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor method to retrieve the Command Descriptor Block associated with the specified request.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool GetCommandDescriptorBlock (
 SCSITaskIdentifierrequest, 
 SCSICommandDescriptorBlock *cdbData ); 
```

## Parameters

- `request`: A valid SCSITaskIdentifier.
- `cdbData`: A pointer to SCSICommandDescriptorBlock to be filled in by this method. NOTE: This routine will always fill in 16 bytes, so if the protocol layer driver supports less than this amount it will have to create a local SCSICommandDescriptorBlock variable to get the CDB data.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

True on success, otherwise false.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Accessor method to retrieve the Command Descriptor Block associated with the specified request.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# GetInitialPowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

This method is called once, right after InitializePowerManagement() in order to determine what state the device is initially in at startup time (usually the highest power mode).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual UInt32 GetInitialPowerState (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The power state the device is currently in.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called once, right after InitializePowerManagement() in order to determine what state the device is initially in at startup time (usually the highest power mode).

# HandleAbortTask

**Interface language:** Objective-C

HandleAbortTask instructs the Protocol Services driver to abort the task.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SCSIServiceResponse HandleAbortTask ( 
 UInt8theLogicalUnit, 
 SCSITaggedTaskIdentifiertheTag ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theLogicalUnit`: A valid logical unit number.
- `theTag`: The tag of the command to abort.

# Document: HandleCheckPowerState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolservices/1810080-handlecheckpowerstate
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolservices/1810080-handlecheckpowerstate
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# HandleCheckPowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Method called to check if the device is in the correct power state for an I/O.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandleCheckPowerState (
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The HandleCheckPowerState (void) method is on the serialized side of the command gate and can change member variables safely without multi-threading issues. Its main purpose is to call the superclass' HandleCheckPowerState ( UInt32 maxPowerState ) with the max power state with which the class registered.

# HandlePowerChange

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

This method is called to handle a power change.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void HandlePowerChange (
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called to handle a power change. It is called from a clean thread context (i.e. new thread, no locks held) and can make synchronous or asynchronous calls.

# HandlePowerOff

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power off call (called on the way to sleep).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn HandlePowerOff (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A valid IOReturn code.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power off call (called on the way to sleep). This method is guaranteed to be called after application layer drivers have been put to sleep.

Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioscsiprotocolservices/1810154-handlepoweron
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# HandlePowerOn

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power on call (called on the way back up from sleep).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn HandlePowerOn (
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A valid IOReturn code.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Convenience method for a protocol service driver to handle a power on call (called on the way back up from sleep). Driver should perform any bus specific activity necessary to recover from power-on/wake from sleep (e.g. bus reset on ATAPI). This method is guaranteed to be called before application layer drivers have been awakened.

# HandleProtocolServiceFeature

HandleProtocolServiceFeature instructs the Protocol Services driver to perform the necessary tasks for the indicated feature.

```objectivec
virtual bool HandleProtocolServiceFeature (
 SCSIProtocolFeaturefeature,
 void *serviceValue ) = 0; 
```

- `feature`: A valid SCSIProtocolFeature.

## Overview

HandleProtocolServiceFeature instructs the Protocol Services driver to perform the necessary tasks for the indicated feature.
